subject.title: improve(build): reuse tsdown declarations across full builds

question: Should coarse-restored declaration reuse be enabled immediately in the npm and macOS release workflows, or staged in CI first?
rationale: The implementation has strong local and Blacksmith proof, but release jobs would consume reusable declaration outputs whose safety depends on the completeness of the new fingerprint contract.

options.title: Keep Release Opt-Ins
options.body: Retain the current release-workflow scope after current-head cross-key proof confirms byte-identical declarations for both unrelated and declaration-relevant changes.

options.title: Stage CI-Only
options.body: Enable reuse in ordinary CI first and add npm/macOS release opt-ins after several successful cache generations or dedicated release-lane proof.

options.title: Defer Declaration Reuse
options.body: Keep release and CI full builds uncached until maintainers are comfortable owning the long-term fingerprint input contract.

recommendation.title: Keep Release Opt-Ins
recommendation.body: Retain the current release-workflow scope after current-head cross-key proof confirms byte-identical declarations for both unrelated and declaration-relevant changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior merged build-cache work and the current proposal both originate from this owner, giving them the strongest context for the intended release-safety boundary.
